subject: Accounting
title: The General Journal
description: A 60-second lesson on The General Journal.

hook.text: The general journal is the company's diary—every financial event recorded in date order.

buildup.text: Each entry includes the date, accounts affected, amounts, and a brief description.

discovery.text: The journal is the first place transactions are recorded—before they move to the ledger.

twist.text: In modern software, journal entry and ledger posting happen simultaneously—but the logic is the same.

climax.text: A well-maintained journal creates a complete, chronological trail of every financial event.

punchline.text: The journal tells the story of money, day by day.

quiz.question: What is the general journal?
options: A chronological record of all financial transactions

details.summary: The general journal is the book of original entry where all financial transactions are first recorded in chronological order. This topic explains journal entry format—date, accounts, debits, credits, and narration—and how the journal feeds the rest of the bookkeeping system.
details.whyItMatters: The general journal is where bookkeeping begins. Every transaction passes through it first, making it the foundational record from which all other financial reports are built.
takeaways: Each journal entry includes the date, accounts debited and credited, amounts, and a brief narration
Entries are recorded in chronological order as transactions occur
The general journal captures transactions that don't fit into special journals

faq.question: What is the general journal in bookkeeping?
faq.answer: The general journal is the primary record where financial transactions are first recorded in date order. Each entry consists of the transaction date, accounts to debit and credit, dollar amounts, and a brief explanation of what happened.

faq.question: What is the difference between the general journal and the general ledger?
faq.answer: The general journal records transactions in chronological order as they happen. The general ledger organizes the same data by account, showing all activity and balances for each account. Data flows from journal to ledger through the posting process.
